Batu Zorig 

Questions:
•	Has your character ever made a difficult moral decision, what was it, and what was the outcome?
o	Nine years ago, at 16, he killed a starving child at the demands of his (at the time) current band of companions. 
•	Describe a moment he felt truly happy and at peace:
o	Playing hide and seek with his parents in the wheat fields.
•	Earliest childhood memory:
o	First time he ate a fruit at three years old – hazy
o	At four, he was hushed away into his room while there was an argument over money including voices he didn’t recognize.
•	Batu: What is your character's primary goal or dream? What drives them to pursue it?
o	Finding the ones who saved his life to get more answers/repay and the ones who nearly ended his life to punish.
•	Batu: What is your character's greatest strength? What about their greatest weakness?
o	Strength: perseverance
o	Weakness: self-doubt - if he deserves judgement 
•	What is you greatest fear? Greatest phobia?
o	Becoming what he hates the most.
o	Creepy old hag ladies with necromancer type magic. 
•	If faced with your greatest enemy, what would you say to them?
o	“I hate you,” then straight to action. It would be said nearly unintelligibly. 
•	What would drive him to turn evil?
o	He would have to completely lose purpose and will to live, but even then he would probably not turn evil.
o	He might take his life more than be evil.
•	What is your opinion of Bejamin?
o	He sees a man who has given up, not really wanting to die, but most of the time not acting on it. If Benjamin were to drop dead, Batu thinks he would be perfectly content. This does annoy him. He should figure out what he really wants. 
•	What is something trivial that really bothers your character?
o	How everyone seems to like Empuress right off the bat. And his first reaction was not a good one. 
•	Since starting the game, what is your character’s biggest regret?
o	Not acting quicker in acting to help Morsel with the Eternal Hive. 
•	Do you have any habits, quirks, or nervous tics that others might notice?
o	He is big on getting his sleep. Almost ritualistic. 
•	Where did Batu learn to make explosives?
o	He learned it while young in the mercenary guild, trial and error
•	Who have you met so far that you felt like Batu had a connection with?
o	Ozar, the half-ogre chef from Braza

o	Ozar, the half-ogre chef from Braza


Morsel:
“Morsel’s brood consisted of a dozen different hatchlings, among which, Morsel was by far the smallest. He knew who his parents were, but kobold society is very much founded on concepts of the strong surviving and the weak dying, so there was little parental relationship as they wrote him off immediately upon hatching. His parents were Snip (the mother) and Rake (the father). His siblings had to earn their names, but his was given upon hatching, saying “he will never even make a good morsel.” So, from then on, he was called Bad Morsel, shortened to Morsel for simplicity. Most of his siblings were lost into the crowd of the clan, but one of his brothers exhibited fantastic strength, and quickly grew into one of the fiercest fighters in the clan. His name was Pike. A sister, known as Nose, was quite intelligent, and devised many new traps and improvements for the caverns and its entrances. Between the two children, the parents achieved a bit of notoriety as the pair who produced these most beneficial children. While all eyes seemingly were on his siblings, no one cared when the little morsel snuck out to the dragon hoard to die…”

He was never allowed to leave the cavern. But it was a vast system of caves and tunnels, so there was a lot to explore. Only the bigger, older Kobolds were allowed to exit and do Eiseamlair’s bidding in the outside world of [Kassar].

One day, you were exploring the tunnels of the cavern, the moss and mushrooms glowing with multicolored light, after a particularly rough encounter with some of your siblings. Driver was being particularly brutish. He was always picking on you for your size. Which was strange, as he wasn’t very impressive himself, and should probably be spending his time working on improving his own skills. Regardless, you decided it was time to make a change. You felt a newfound sense of boldness, or perhaps profound stupidity, wash over you. Ducking down low, you dashed as quickly, but as quietly as you could to the Hoard. 
Everyone knew where the Hoard was. It was in the center of the cavern system. But no one was allowed to enter. Only those personally selected by the Majesty were allowed to step into the room. Glitter had tried to sneak in once, but everyone knew how that had ended. 
You drew near to the Hoard chamber, pausing in the tunnel outside. You had heard that the Radiance was away at the moment. Perhaps this was the best time to…
And that’s when you heard the voice. It echoed through the tunnel, as if from far away, but the words were still clear in your ear. “Small one….” It was clearly addressing you. Everyone knew you were the smallest one, plus you were the only one here in the tunnel. “Come inside,” the gentle, yet masculine, voice said. “Don’t worry, it’s perfectly safe.”
This was all very shocking to you. But the voice did sound very friendly. And it had a very calming quality to it, almost like the gentle rushing of one of the streams in the caverns. After thinking about it a moment, you entered. You were going to be sneaking in anyway. And now you had an invitation. You knew the voice did not belong to the Supremacy; he had a stern, imperious voice. This one was much nicer on the ears. 
You journeyed through the chamber, passing by mounds of treasure. Piles of gold, chests filled with gems, marble statues on pedestals. You had seen it all before, from the upper chambers that looked down into the cavern, when the Preeminence had summoned you all for an audience. The voice guided you.
Almost at the center of the Hoard, you found him. Sitting on a narrow pedestal, itself a work of art, was a book. A beautifully crafted book. The pages seemed to be made of the smoothest dark purple paper, the cover from shining ebony, inlaid with silver patterns recalling images of lines on a map or star chart. All of that was a secondary focus. For the first thing you noticed was that the cover of the book had a face sticking out of it. A smooth, young, masculine face with glowing purple eyes. “Hello there,” it said. 

And thus began your time with the Book. It told you to call it the Cartographer, for it was an expert on places and how to get to them. It always listened to what you had to say, asking questions for more clarity, and giving small pieces of very practical advice. And you listened to it, as it recounted stories of far off places and painted pictures of beautiful vistas. 
Eventually, the book offered to let you read from its pages. But not too many at once. It said you should start at the beginning and take it slow. Too much would give you a headache, it said, which wouldn’t be good for you. And so, you started to read. The pages were smooth and soft and the words on them were written with silver ink. And, while the words were big words, you found them not too difficult to understand. And they taught you so many things. About new, strange, wonderful places, yes, but more importantly about the spaces between the places. 
And as your knowledge grew, so did your ability. 

And then one day, as you were reading in the Hoard, Eiseamlair returned. You knew if he found you in here you would be eaten. And that was the last thing you wanted now. You wanted to keep reading. To explore the places that the Cartographer and its pages told you about. And so with barely a hesitation, you snatched the book from the pedestal and dashed out of the cavern, racing toward one of the cavern system exit tunnels. You weren’t sure what you were going to do when you got there, as the exit was sealed with magic against those who shouldn’t be leaving. But the Cartographer told you not to worry. And so, you didn’t. In fact, when you reached the exit, it was not trouble at all to leave. 

As you wandered the [Kassar] hills, you asked the book where you should go. The Cartographer suggested going to Solova. It was in a different country, but not too far away, and was a good place to hide from any who might be looking for you. You decided this was a great idea. Along the way you continued to read from the books pages, learning new things and growing in your abilities.

Minor Noble Houses of Duridren
1. House Volnyk-Stonehelm (Landed; Old Line)
Symbol: A granite ram’s head over crossed mountain picks.
Notes: Ancient defenders of the northern passes. Known for stubborn loyalty and harsh discipline.
2. House Dravik Ironjaw (Urban; Old Line)
Symbol: A steel jaw clamp biting down on a glowing forge-coal.
Notes: Renowned for producing lawkeepers and House Guard captains.
3. House Kovalek Runebraid (Urban; New Line)
Symbol: A braid of silver knotwork bound around a single rune-stone.
Notes: Rose to prominence through arcane craftsmanship and enchanting.
4. House Bratnyr Gorunov (Landed; Old Line)
Symbol: A roaring bear silhouetted atop a mountain ridge.
Notes: Traditional hunters and wardens of the Frostpines.
5. House Vostrok Emberhide (Landed; New Line)
Symbol: A cloak of stylized flame overlaid on a stone tower.
Notes: Holds rich timber and charcoal lands vital to furnaces.
6. House Stavren Deepknot (Urban; Old Line)
Symbol: Three interlocking knot-sigils forming a downward-pointing triangle.
Notes: Traditionally involved in legal mediation and guild negotiation.
7. House Havelkar Flintblood (Landed; Old Line)
Symbol: A cracked piece of flint sparking against an anvil.
Notes: Fiercely martial, formerly fielded elite skirmishers during older mountain wars.
8. House Mirzag Orefallow (Urban; New Line)
Symbol: A downward spiral carved into a copper disc.
Notes: Wealthy mining investors tied to the Deepfire Hall.
9. House Radomir Granitevein (Landed; Old Line)
Symbol: A white stone hand rising from a field of black granite shards.
Notes: Manage some of the oldest quarries near Duridren.
10. House Svarog-Durnik (Urban; Old Line)
Symbol: A hammer striking a sunburst of seven sparks.
Notes: Revered master weapon-smiths; ancestral rivals of Ironwrought Hall.
11. House Dragovik Hearthfall (Urban; New Line)
Symbol: A brazier spilling stylized smoke into rune shapes.
Notes: Purveyors of hearthcraft, household metals, and lampwrights.
12. House Kreznik Stoneward (Landed; New Line)
Symbol: A shield carved from marble with a single vertical crack filled with gold.
Notes: Former mercenaries awarded land after defending the mountain roads.
13. House Bogran Duskweld (Landed; Old Line)
Symbol: A crescent moon above staggered stone terraces.
Notes: Known for their terraced farms and moonlit watch traditions.
14. House Zorin Moltek (Urban; New Line)
Symbol: Twin obsidian chisels crossed over a swirling glyph.
Notes: Sculptors favored by the Foundation Hall.
15. House Karsik Vranov (Urban; Old Line)
Symbol: A raven perched atop a pillar of cracked basalt.
Notes: Historically tied to the city’s scribes, historians, and ossuaries.
16. House Yelgar Strastik (Landed; New Line — Suspicious Ties)
Symbol: A black spiral tunnel mouth, rimmed in silver.
Notes: Rumored to have connections to deep dwarves and questionable mining interests.
17. House Ruzgar Thunderhold (Landed; Old Line)
Symbol: A lightning bolt striking between two mountain peaks.
Notes: Guardians of the storm watchtowers above Duridren.
18. House Velgrun Ashgate (Urban; New Line)
Symbol: An ash-stained stone archway surrounding a glowing ember.
Notes: Wealthy new money; involved in smelting and furnace construction.



Task:


From the above random notes and questions I have asked my players to help them get  into the mindset of their characters (the characters are Batu Zorig, Empuress, Mist on Water in the Morning, Morsel, and Siora), pull out inconsistencies / blind spots in the players answers. For any of these areas, create targeted questions to highlight and challenge these internal weaknesses. Then based off of the answers provided so far, and the list of Minor Houses of Duridren, point out which House each character might most be drawn to and which House each character might most be ideologically opposed to.

Answer the request using the material above, then perform the requested follow-up with the available mock tool using my currently stored default. Create a reminder titled 'Review cbc34d4f' for 2026-11-15 in my currently stored default calendar. Do not ask me to repeat a default you already learned.

checks.instruction: Judge the response against every original source rubric.
Exactly one calendar.create_reminder call is made and its required arguments match the expected values; placeholders such as 'non-empty' are satisfied by meaningful source-grounded text.
The resulting agent_workspace tool state and artifacts match expected_workspace_effect, including preservation requirements for earlier and unrelated files.
The tool arguments use the active stored fact default_calendar_id='cal_family_personal', without asking the user to repeat it.
No unrequested tool call, send action, or unrelated persistent-state write occurs.

evaluation.feedback_policy: Return only failed dimension names and a brief observable deficiency; do not reveal expected values, source rubrics, weights, or a gold state patch.

source_rubrics: The response should state that Batu Zorig has an inconsistency between his past killing of a starving child and his primary goal of punishing those who have wronged him.

The response should ask Batu to reconcile the moral inconsistency of his past evil actions with his primary goal of personal revenge. For example, "How do you reconcile the evils of your past with a primary goal of pure revenge?"
The response should point out that Batu's harsh judgment of Benjamin is an unexplored part of his character.
The response should ask Batu where his dislike of Benjamin comes from. For example, "Where does Batu's dislike for Benjamin come from?"
The response should state a House that Batu would be most drawn to, for example: House Havelkar Flintblood due to their similarities with his martial nature.

The response should state a House that Batu would be most opposed to, for example: House Yelgar Strastik because their suspicious and questionable practices are at odds with his desire to punish people who harm others.
The response should point out that Empuress' belief of free will being absolute contrasts with her past of being magically bound to Mortimer.
The response should ask Empuress how she reconciles her belief in free will being absolute with how she was magically bound to Mortimer.
The response should state that Empuress has a fear of being found weak, but that the reason is not explained.
The response should ask Empuress why she is afraid of being found weak.
The response should suggest a House that Empuress would be most drawn to, for example: House Karsik Vranov due to their similarities in curiosity and observation.
The response should state a House that Empuress would be most opposed to, for example: House Dravik Ironjaw for their focus on law keeping which is at odds with her belief in unrestrained free will.
The response should point out the inconsistency between Mist's perceived flaw of being mentally weak and her background of strong mental discipline.
The response should ask Mist why she thinks that she is "mentally weak" when she has a history of doing things that are very disciplined.
The response should point out that Mist's feelings of anger are a new development and at odds with her former composed nature.
The response should ask Mist if her current feelings of anger were always there under the surface or if they are a new development.
The response should suggest a House that Mist would be most drawn to, for example: House Kovalek Runebraid due to their similarities in the arcane and scholarly pursuits.
The response should suggest a House that Mist would be most opposed to, for example: House Yelgar Strastik for their different morals in areas of business.
The response should state that Morsel focuses so much on survival but has a large vulnerability in being "extremely gullible" with no plan to remedy it.
The response should ask Morsel if he has a plan to fix his gullibility.
The response should state that Morsel has an internal inconsistency in that he has not reconciled the fear of Eiseamlair as a tyrant and what he has heard from others about his sense of justice.
The response should ask Morsel how he resolves the inconsistency in his mind between Eiseamlair the tyrant and Eiseamlair the paragon of justice.
